Plain Text Notes Last Forever

By Mira Okafor and Jonas Lind

Every note app eventually goes away. The files it wrote do not have to. When your notes are plain Markdown files on your own disk, any editor written in the next fifty years can open them, and a+b still means a+b.

Files outlive formats

Proprietary databases tie your thinking to a vendor's roadmap. A folder of text files ties it to nothing at all. You can search it with grep, sync it with anything, and read it on a machine that has never heard of the app.

  • Open with any editor
  • Version with git
  • Back up by copying

Tip

Keep attachments next to the notes that use them.

A small habit

Write the date at the top of each note. It costs nothing and turns a pile of files into a timeline you can walk back through years later. 

grep -rl "plain text" ~/Notes

The best format for a note you want to read in twenty years is the one that needs nothing but your eyes to read it today.
